neighbours.label: A neck or trunk location on the body (neck, throat, chest, waist) where a garment, strap or sensation sits; the + pole takes the limbs
fire: The gown fastens with a single pearl button at the back of the neck.
Pull the upper strap tight across the chest before you clip the buckle.
The apron ties at the waist and has a loop that goes over the head.
She wore a thin gold locket around her neck every day.
The sweater felt tight at the throat and loose everywhere else.
A wide sash was wrapped twice around the waist of the robe.
The medal hung on a ribbon and rested against his chest.
The collar of the shirt left a red mark on his neck.
quiet: The glove fastens with a single pearl button at the back of the wrist.
Pull the lower strap tight across the ankle before you clip the buckle.
The sleeve ends at the elbow and has a loop that goes over the thumb.
She wore a thin gold bracelet around her wrist every day.
The boot felt tight at the heel and loose everywhere else.
A wide bandage was wrapped twice around the knee of the runner.
The watch hung on a strap and rested against his forearm.
The cuff of the shirt left a red mark on his hand.

notes: Card: ' body', ' neck', ' around' (my neck), ' waist', ' chest', neckline, French 'col'; the + pole peaks on limb contexts (amputate, cuffs, legs, wheel) and its output promotes ' leg', ' limbs', ' ankles'. So the neuron seems to split trunk from limbs. Probes: neck 1.10 and 0.74, chest 0.68, throat 0.49, waist 0.43; cuffs / elbows 0.07, ankle / knee 0.00, fingers / wrists / shins 0.03. ' body' as a general noun was weak (0.05-0.13) and shoulders / back 0.05.
